objective: Exercise the pipeline end to end on a transverse-field Ising quench: does the lattice-averaged occupation <n> relax towards the plateau the noise model predicts at hx/J = 6?

paper.title: Transverse-field Ising quench on a square Rydberg lattice

builder_params.spacing_note: derived from hx, omega and C6 by the builder, not fixed here

observable.description: lattice-averaged Rydberg occupation <n> vs quench duration

open_questions.question: the original run scanned 75 time points in one parametric batch; 10 are kept here because this pipeline submits one batch per point. Is 10 enough to resolve the approach to the plateau?
open_questions.why: 10 batches x 300 shots is the smallest scan that still shows the relaxation
open_questions.impact: sets the time resolution; more points cost proportionally more QPU shots

open_questions.question: hx/J = 6 was chosen because the noise model tracks hardware best there, not because the physics is most interesting there. Keep it, or move closer to the critical point?
open_questions.why: this case exists to validate the pipeline, so agreement with the noise model is the point
open_questions.impact: nearer criticality the quench is more sensitive to noise and a QPU-vs-EMU disagreement gets harder to attribute

_notes: hx/J = 6 is the paramagnetic regime, where the FC1 noise model tracks hardware most closely — the reason this case was used to validate the pipeline. The lattice spacing is not a free parameter: the builder derives it from hx, omega and the live C6 so that the interaction sets the requested hx/J. The original submission scanned 75 time points in a single parametric batch; this spec uses 10 points because the pipeline submits one batch per scan point.
